title: RC-B: extend rc8probe.c (independent codebase) with a prefix counter and an ideal-permutation mode
claim_tier_basis: Reduced-round AES-shaped SPN, C1 convention, r=5, one machine, one key per arm, random S-boxes, trials from 2^24 to 2^27. No crypto-scale, medium-scale, affected-scheme or asymptotic claim is made or implied; no comparison to published cryptanalysis in either direction.

certificate.note: Pure measurement task. No discrete-log solve or factor-base relation is claimed anywhere in this task.

STEP3_IDEAL_PERMUTATION.description: Independently re-derived from ledger/evidence/EV-AES-e4c091.yaml OBS-B9-2's specification text (a lazily-sampled uniform random bijection on 128 bits, realised with exactly four oracle queries per trial: forward draws with injectivity-rejection on the output, inverse draws with exact domain-exclusion on the input), NOT by reading BATCH-009's yoyo_sbox_v4.c. Implemented as: (1) a blk128 128-bit value type; (2) an open-addressed hash-indexed pair table (perm128) storing realised (domain,range) pairs with two index tables (dom_idx, rng_idx) resolved by full 128-bit compare (hash collisions never silently accepted as equal); (3) perm128_forward/perm128_inverse implementing the rejection-sampling and domain-exclusion rules exactly as specified; (4) a new single-threaded run_ideal() trial loop reusing rc8probe's own PW/CW geometry and plaintext/active-word draw code (re-typed into the new function, not by editing worker()); (5) a new 'armideal' CLI mode dispatched before the pre-existing arm-mode guard; (6) a new 'permcheck' CLI mode as an independent correctness control.
STEP3_IDEAL_PERMUTATION.additions_only_verdict: CONFIRMED. grep -E '^-[^-]' against the unified diff (excluding the '--- a/file' header line) returns zero matches.

correctness_control.mode: permcheck (new, independent of the yoyo trial harness -- exercises perm128 directly)
properties_checked: round-trip: perm128_inverse(perm128_forward(x)) == x, for 200000 fresh forward-drawn x
idempotence: repeated perm128_forward(x) on an already-queried x returns the identical y (no fresh draw)
pairwise distinctness of all 200000 queried domain points (O(M^2) exact scan)
pairwise distinctness of all 200000 queried range points (O(M^2) exact scan) -- i.e. the realised partial function is injective on the queried domain
cross case: perm128_forward(perm128_inverse(y)) == y, for 20000 fresh inverse-drawn y never previously forward-queried
correctness_control.verdict: The construction satisfies the required properties of a lazily-sampled bijection (round-trip correctness both directions, injectivity on the realised subset, idempotent caching) on this direct test, independent of the yoyo geometry code. This is a re-derivation of the required properties, not a line-by-line comparison to yoyo_sbox_v4.c, which was not read for this task.

The observed k4 count (2, against a 0.125 model) is DIRECTIONALLY consistent with BATCH-008's reported elevation at k=4, but this single run at this exposure cannot and does not establish that on its own; the campaign's own k=4 finding rests on much larger N (2^30) with ~13-14 excess events, not reproduced or refuted at this scale.

COMPARISON_B_IDEAL_VS_LIVE_R5.mirrors: BATCH-009 / EV-AES-e4c091 OBS-B9-3 (the r=5 excess does not survive cipher substitution to an ideal-permutation null object)

seed_thread_match.verdict: IDENTICAL by construction. arm mode with threads=1 computes seed_thread = seed ^ (armid*C1) ^ (1*C2); armideal computes seed_thread = seed ^ (armid*C1) ^ C2. These are the same value when threads=1. Confirmed by direct comparison of the two printed seed_thread fields, not merely by formula inspection.

matched_exposure_construction.plaintext_stream_identity_basis: CODE-LEVEL ARGUMENT ONLY, not independently verified by a digest-based run comparison. worker() (live arm) and run_ideal() draw p0 via two sm64() calls in the same order and apply the same PW-indexed active-word rejection loop for amask; given identical seed_thread, these draws are bit-identical up to the point of the first cipher/oracle call. This was checked by reading the two functions side by side (see src/rc8probe_ideal.c), not by an instrumented run that dumps and diffs the intermediate plaintext streams -- BATCH-009's OBS-B9-3 did run such a digest-based check and this task did not, for budget reasons. Disclosed as a gap below; this task's matched-exposure claim rests on the weaker (but still checkable) code-identity argument, not an executed proof.

preregistered_decision_rule_applied.expected_result_at_this_exposure: Preregistered as the LIKELY outcome: BATCH-009's ~14-hit live-arm excess at N=2^30 scales to ~14/64 ~ 0.22 expected excess events at N=2^24 -- almost certainly 0 or 1 observed hit, insufficient to distinguish confirm from disconfirm.
preregistered_decision_rule_applied.observed: 0 hits in BOTH the live and ideal-permutation arms.
preregistered_decision_rule_applied.verdict: INCONCLUSIVE BY POWER, exactly as preregistered before running. Neither arm shows any elevation over its own (identical, 0.015625) null expectation at this exposure -- there is nothing to compare a 'live elevation' against an 'ideal elevation' when both raw counts are zero. This is NOT read as confirming BATCH-009 (a null result in the live arm alone does not establish that an excess exists to be extinguished) and NOT read as refuting it (a null result in the ideal arm is exactly what BATCH-009 also predicts). The comparison, as run at this exposure, settles nothing about the mechanism claim either way.

OUTCOME_SUMMARY.shared_harness_risk_named_by_batch_010: NOT resolved by this task. Comparison (a)'s well-powered sub-claim (byte-locality absence at k=1-3) DID replicate on an independent substrate, which is evidence against a shared-harness explanation for THAT specific sub-finding. Comparison (b), which is the more direct test of the shared-harness concern (cipher substitution should extinguish an artifact but not a real cipher-shape effect), produced no informative signal at the budget-permitted exposure -- it neither corroborates nor contradicts BATCH-009's finding on this substrate. The residual risk BATCH-010 named for the cipher-substitution mechanism claim specifically is therefore UNCHANGED by this task, not closed; it would need either a larger budget (to reach an exposure where the ideal-permutation arm's memory footprint and the expected event count both become tractable) or a different implementation strategy for the permutation table.

FINDING: Two disjoint outcomes on one independent substrate: BATCH-008's well-powered byte-locality sub-claim (no excess at k=1,2,3) replicated; BATCH-009's cipher-substitution comparison produced a zero-information null (0 vs 0) at the budget-permitted exposure and settles nothing. PROTOCOL_DEVIATIONS_AND_INCIDENTS: No timeouts, crashes, or OOM events occurred during any of the four timed measurement runs or the earlier smoke/correctness tests. All processes exited 0.

The armideal run's memory footprint was estimated from allocation-size arithmetic in the code, not measured with a peak-RSS profiling tool (e.g. /usr/bin/time -v or a cgroup memory.max_usage_in_bytes read). This is a real gap, disclosed rather than silently assumed away; `free -h` was checked once immediately before the run and showed 12Gi free, giving informal confidence the ~4.3GB estimate would not exhaust the 8GB budget, but this is not the same as a measured peak.

The comparison-(b) matched-plaintext-stream claim rests on a code-level argument (both functions draw identically given identical seed_thread), not on an executed digest-based comparison of the actual intermediate streams, unlike BATCH-009's own OBS-B9-3 which did run such a check. Named explicitly in PREREGISTRATION.md before measurement and repeated here.

Background-tool timeouts: two of the timed runs (STEP1's 2^30 reproduction, ~236s, and STEP2's 2^30 equivalence rebuild, ~236s) exceeded this environment's 120-second foreground command timeout and were moved to background execution by the harness; both completed normally (exit 0) and their outputs were read from the completed background task. This is an infrastructure/tooling mechanic, not a run failure, and is recorded here for completeness -- no data was lost or altered by the backgrounding.

No claim is made about AES, full-round AES, or any deployed cryptographic scheme.

No claim is made that the ideal-permutation construction here is identical in code to yoyo_sbox_v4.c's implementation -- it was independently derived from the OBS-B9-2 specification text and independently verified via permcheck, not compared line-by-line to v4.c, which was deliberately not read for this task.
